question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x) & =15 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x) & =\frac{15}{5} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The logarithm is a natural logarithm, which means its base is $e.$ So, we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x) & =3 \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)} & ={e}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}=2x.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={e}^{3} \\ x & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
